content.text:
I can’t open or edit attachments from this chat (no spreadsheet tool or file was provided here), so I did not and cannot make any changes to your workbook.

Concrete next steps you can take (pick one):

Option A — I help you with exact edits if you paste data here
- Paste the sheet header row plus ~10 representative rows (including any columns that contain formulas) into the chat. I’ll give step‑by‑step changes you can run locally that preserve formulas and structure.

Option B — Run this safe, local checklist yourself (keeps formulas intact)
1. Make a full backup copy of the workbook/file.
2. Identify which cells/columns contain formulas:
   - Excel: Home → Find & Select → Go To Special → Formulas (or press Ctrl+` to view formulas).
   - Google Sheets: View → Show formulas (or Ctrl+~).
   Mark or note those columns so you do not delete formula cells unintentionally.
3. Add a helper column "DedupeKey" (temporary) that concatenates the unique identifying fields (example template — edit column letters to match your sheet):
   - =TRIM($A2)&"|"&LOWER(TRIM($B2))&"|"&TRIM($C2)
   This produces a consistent key for duplicate detection.
4. Flag duplicates (keep first occurrence) with a helper formula (put in another helper column):
   - =IF(COUNTIF($D$2:D2,D2)>1,"Duplicate","Keep")
   (Adjust D to your DedupeKey column.)
5. Remove duplicates while preserving formulas:
   - Preferred safe method: Filter the helper column for "Keep", select visible rows, copy → Paste into a new sheet (Paste as Values for data-only). This produces a cleaned sheet without touching original formulas.
   - If you must remove duplicate rows in-place: filter to show "Duplicate", then with the filtered range selected use Home → Find & Select → Go To Special → Constants, then Clear Contents. That clears only non-formula cells in the filtered duplicates and leaves any formula cells intact. (Do NOT delete rows if your workbook uses row-based formulas elsewhere — deletions can break relative references.)
6. Fix broken date formats:
   - Identify text dates: create helper column =ISTEXT(A2) or attempt =DATEVALUE(A2).
   - Convert safely:
     - Excel quick: select the date column → Data → Text to Columns → Next → Next → Column data format: Date (choose correct order) → Finish. This converts text to real dates without touching formulas.
     - Or use helper formula: =IFERROR(DATEVALUE(TRIM(A2)), "") or parse with DATE/LEFT/MID/RIGHT if needed. Once verified, paste converted dates back over original using Paste Special → Values.
   - Google Sheets: use =VALUE(A2) or =DATEVALUE(A2), verify results, then Paste values over originals.
7. Verify:
   - Check for #VALUE! or changed cells.
   - Remove helper columns after confirming everything is correct.

Option C — I can provide a short VBA macro (run locally) that:
- Makes a backup sheet,
- Adds a dedupe key,
- Flags duplicates,
- Clears non-formula cells in duplicate rows (preserving formula cells),
- Attempts safe date conversions for text dates into true Date values.

If you want the VBA macro, say “Give VBA” and tell me which columns are the identifying keys (e.g., CustomerID in A, Email in C) and which column(s) contain date strings.

Which option do you want to proceed with?
